setting.world: Real-world historical England with no fantasy elements
setting.description: Late-Victorian England centered on London lodgings at 221B Baker Street and extending to country houses, villages, banks, hotels and railway suburbs. A gas-lit world of hansom cabs, broughams, telegrams, pawnshops, opium dens, and manor houses where respectable society conceals crime.

characters.name: Sherlock Holmes
characters.physical_description: Tall, spare man with a long, nervous face, keen grey eyes, and thin hawk-like nose. Typically wears a dressing-gown at home and dresses respectably in tweed when out.

characters.name: John Watson
characters.physical_description: Average-built middle-aged man with a moustache, of military neatness. Typically wears a top-hat, frock-coat, and carries a stethoscope.

characters.name: Irene Adler
characters.physical_description: Beautiful woman with a superb figure, dark hair, and a lovely face. Often seen in evening dress or walking clothes, and later in male costume as a slim youth in an ulster.

characters.name: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond von Ormstein
characters.physical_description: Gigantic man over six feet six inches tall with the chest and limbs of a Hercules, thick hanging lip, and long straight chin. Wears a rich double-breasted coat slashed with astrakhan, flame-silk-lined blue cloak, fur-trimmed high boots, and initially a black vizard mask.

characters.name: Godfrey Norton
characters.physical_description: Remarkably handsome man, dark, aquiline, and moustached, dashing in appearance. Typically wears a lawyer's dark suit.

characters.name: Jabez Wilson
characters.physical_description: Stout, florid-faced, elderly gentleman with fiery blazing red hair. Wears baggy grey shepherd's check trousers, black frock-coat, drab waistcoat with brassy Albert chain, frayed top-hat and faded brown overcoat with wrinkled velvet collar.

characters.name: Vincent Spaulding
characters.physical_description: Small, stout-built man in his thirties, very quick in his ways, clean-shaven with no hair on his face. Has a white splash of acid on his forehead and pierced ears for earrings.

characters.name: Duncan Ross
characters.physical_description: Small man with a head even redder than Wilson's bright red hair. Dresses in a plain office suit.

characters.name: Peter Jones
characters.physical_description: Bulky official police agent with a consequential manner. Wears standard plain Victorian detective's dress.

characters.name: Alexander Merryweather
characters.physical_description: Long, thin, sad-faced elderly gentleman with a very shiny hat. Wears an oppressively respectable frock-coat.

characters.name: Mary Sutherland
characters.physical_description: Large nervous woman with a broad good-humoured face, short-sighted eyes, and brickish-red feather in a broad-brimmed slate-coloured straw hat. Wears a black jacket with beads and jet fringe, brown dress with purple plush, greyish gloves, gold earrings, and mismatched half-buttoned boots.

characters.name: James Windibank
characters.physical_description: Sturdy middle-sized man about thirty, clean-shaven and sallow-skinned with wonderfully sharp penetrating grey eyes. In disguise wears bushy black side-whiskers and moustache, tinted glasses, black frock-coat faced with silk, grey Harris tweed trousers and brown gaiters.

characters.name: James McCarthy
characters.physical_description: Comely lad of eighteen, well-built. Typically wears country clothes and at the time of the incident carries a gun.

characters.name: Charles McCarthy
characters.physical_description: Middle-aged Australian man, cold and forbidding in manner. Wears typical farmer's country dress.

characters.name: John Turner
characters.physical_description: Giant elderly man about sixty with enormous limbs, hard deep-lined craggy features, tangled beard, grizzled hair and drooping eyebrows, ash-white face. Walks with a slow limping step and wears thick-soled shooting-boots and a grey cloak.

characters.name: Alice Turner
characters.physical_description: Very lovely young woman of eighteen with violet eyes, parted lips and pink-flushed cheeks. Wears a fashionable young lady's dress.

characters.name: John Openshaw
characters.physical_description: Young man about twenty-two, well-groomed and trimly clad with refinement and delicacy. Wears golden pince-nez, long shining waterproof and carries a streaming umbrella.

characters.name: Elias Openshaw
characters.physical_description: Fierce elderly ex-planter and Confederate colonel, quick-tempered with retiring habits. No distinctive clothing described beyond typical gentleman's rural dress.

characters.name: Neville St. Clair
characters.physical_description: Respectable gentleman with fair features, normally clean-shaven and well-dressed. In disguise as a beggar is filthy with a repulsive scar, twisted lip, red hair, and dirty rags.

characters.name: Mrs. St. Clair
characters.physical_description: Anxious young wife with a sympathetic expressive face. Wears a fashionable Victorian villa dress.

characters.name: Isa Whitney
characters.physical_description: Haggard opium-addicted man, sallow and emaciated with stupor. Wears dishevelled gentleman's clothes.

characters.name: Kate Whitney
characters.physical_description: Veiled young lady who appears distressed and tearful. Wears a veil and typical middle-class lady's dress.

characters.name: Inspector Lestrade
characters.physical_description: Lean, ferret-like, furtive and sly-looking professional detective. Wears a light brown dustcoat and leather leggings in the country.

characters.name: Inspector Bradstreet
characters.physical_description: Official police inspector in uniform tunic. Middle-aged with a professional authoritative bearing.

characters.name: Henry Baker
characters.physical_description: Large, shabby-genteel man with a highly intellectual large head. Wears a battered old hat and worn respectable clothes.

characters.name: James Ryder
characters.physical_description: Cringing rat-faced little man, pale and nervous. Wears an attendant's uniform or common overcoat.

characters.name: Helen Stoner
characters.physical_description: Young lady in black, veiled and trembling, with a mud-spattered sleeve. Pale with frightened eyes, wears a travelling dress.

characters.name: Grimesby Roylott
characters.physical_description: Huge violent man with a large face seared with yellow wrinkles, deep-set eyes and high thin nose. Wears a top-hat, long frock-coat and gaiters.

characters.name: Victor Hatherley
characters.physical_description: Pale young hydraulic engineer with a blood-soaked handkerchief round his hand. Wears a workman's suit and carries an engineer's bag.

characters.name: Lysander Stark
characters.physical_description: Cadaverously thin man with a harsh face and cold manner. Dresses in dark professional clothes.

characters.name: Lord Robert St. Simon
characters.physical_description: Foppish aristocratic man in his forties with aggrieved dignity, aquiline features. Dresses in elegant morning coat, high collar and top-hat.

characters.name: Hatty Doran
characters.physical_description: Young Californian heiress with a tomboyish, spirited look, volcanic resolve. Wears a wedding dress with veil, ulster and bonnet when fleeing.

characters.name: Francis Hay Moulton
characters.physical_description: Sun-browned American young man, rough mining-camp appearance. Wears a common coat and slouch hat.

characters.name: Alexander Holder
characters.physical_description: Tall, portly, richly dressed gentleman of fifty with a distressed face. Wears fine banking clothes.

characters.name: Arthur Holder
characters.physical_description: Young wild-looking gentleman in his shirt, handsome but dissipated. Typically wears evening shirt and trousers, barefoot during the incident.

characters.name: Mary Holder
characters.physical_description: Devoted young niece and housekeeper, pale and grief-stricken with dark hair. Wears a modest house dress.

characters.name: George Burnwell
characters.physical_description: Fascinating handsome aristocratic man with dark dashing looks. Dresses in fashionable clubman's evening clothes.

characters.name: Violet Hunter
characters.physical_description: Young governess with abundant chestnut hair later cut short, bright eager face. Wears a modest dress, later an electric-blue dress.

characters.name: Jephro Rucastle
characters.physical_description: Smiling stout man with a jovial red face and thick appearance. Dresses in country squire's clothes.

chapters.title: A SCANDAL IN BOHEMIA
chapters.summary: The King of Bohemia hires Sherlock Holmes to recover a compromising cabinet photograph from opera singer Irene Adler before his impending marriage. Holmes locates the hiding place with a staged street brawl and fake fire alarm, but Adler, newly married to Godfrey Norton, outwits him by fleeing to the Continent after following him in male disguise. She leaves her own photograph and a letter promising to keep the original only as safeguard, earning Holmes's eternal respect as The Woman.
chapters.cover_description: Irene Adler in evening dress rushing to a hidden recess behind a sliding panel above a bell-pull in her lamplit Victorian sitting-room as fake fire smoke curls through the open window, while Sherlock Holmes disguised as an elderly Nonconformist clergyman with white tie and broad black hat watches her from a sofa.

chapters.title: THE RED-HEADED LEAGUE
chapters.summary: Red-headed pawnbroker Jabez Wilson is paid £4 a week to copy the Encyclopaedia until the League suddenly dissolves. Holmes deduces the job was a ruse by assistant Vincent Spaulding, alias John Clay, to clear Wilson from his shop while tunnelling to the abutting bank. Holmes, Watson, Jones and Merryweather keep night vigil in the vault and arrest Clay and his red-headed accomplice as they break through.
chapters.cover_description: Two thieves break up through the stone floor of a dark bank vault piled with crates of French gold, while Sherlock Holmes flashes a lantern and lunges with his hunting crop beside police and Watson with a cocked revolver.

chapters.title: A CASE OF IDENTITY
chapters.summary: Miss Mary Sutherland consults Holmes about her fiancé Hosmer Angel, who vanished from a cab at the church door on their wedding day after exacting vows of fidelity. Holmes deduces from typewriting defects, disguise clues, and motive that Angel never existed, but was Mary's stepfather James Windibank in whiskers, tinted glasses and a whisper to keep her single and retain her income. He traps Windibank with typewriter evidence, but cannot prosecute him and spares Mary the disillusionment.
chapters.cover_description: A large nervous Victorian woman in a broad-brimmed straw hat with a brick-red feather and fur boa stands perplexed outside a church, while an empty four-wheeler cab waits at the curb where her missing bridegroom in tinted glasses and bushy whiskers has vanished on their wedding morning.

chapters.title: THE BOSCOMBE VALLEY MYSTERY
chapters.summary: Holmes and Watson travel to Herefordshire to investigate the murder of Charles McCarthy at Boscombe Pool, for which his son James stands accused on strong circumstantial evidence. By reading tracks, the dying word Ballarat, and the Australian Cooee signal, Holmes proves the killer was the dying landowner John Turner, once Black Jack of Ballarat, blackmailed by McCarthy. Holmes secures Turner's written confession to save James but keeps it secret unless needed, leading to James's acquittal.
chapters.cover_description: Sherlock Holmes on hands and knees with a lens at the reed-girt Boscombe Pool, tracing footprints in trampled grass beneath a great beech tree while holding a mossy grey stone, the murder weapon.

chapters.title: THE FIVE ORANGE PIPS
chapters.summary: On a stormy September night young John Openshaw asks Holmes for help after his uncle Elias and father Joseph both died mysteriously following letters containing five orange pips and signed K.K.K. Holmes deduces Ku Klux Klan vengeance pursued by men on a sailing ship and urges Openshaw to decoy them with a surviving diary page, but Openshaw is murdered that night near Waterloo Bridge. Holmes traces the killers to the barque Lone Star bound for Savannah and mails them their own pip warning, only f
chapters.cover_description: A pale young man in a shining waterproof with golden pince-nez shakes five dried orange pips from a crumpled envelope onto a table in a lamplit Victorian sitting room, while a tall spare detective and his moustached companion bend forward in the firelight as a violent storm rages at the windows.

chapters.title: THE MAN WITH THE TWISTED LIP
chapters.summary: Watson goes to an East End opium den to rescue Isa Whitney and finds Holmes disguised there investigating the disappearance of Neville St. Clair, supposedly murdered after crying for help from the den window. A letter in St. Clair's hand received after his vanishing convinces his wife he lives, and after a night of thought Holmes takes Watson to Bow Street. Holmes washes the prisoner beggar Hugh Boone's face with a sponge, revealing him as St. Clair himself, who confesses he lived a secret doubl
chapters.cover_description: Sherlock Holmes vigorously sponges the filthy face of the sleeping beggar Hugh Boone in a Bow Street cell, his twisted lip and scar peeling away to reveal the missing gentleman Neville St. Clair as Watson and Inspector Bradstreet watch in astonishment.

chapters.title: THE ADVENTURE OF THE BLUE CARBUNCLE
chapters.summary: What begins as Holmes's playful deduction from a lost hat becomes a jewel theft case when Peterson finds the Countess of Morcar's stolen blue carbuncle in the crop of a Christmas goose dropped by Henry Baker. Holmes proves Baker innocent, traces the goose through the Alpha Inn to Breckinridge to Mrs. Oakshott, and traps head attendant James Ryder, who hid the stone in a goose to frame plumber John Horner. Holmes lets the terrified Ryder flee to let Horner's case collapse in the season of forgive
chapters.cover_description: Sherlock Holmes in his purple dressing-gown holding up a brilliantly sparkling blue carbuncle found in the crop of a Christmas goose, with a battered black felt hat on a chair and a crackling Victorian fireplace at 221B Baker Street.

chapters.title: THE ADVENTURE OF THE SPECKLED BAND
chapters.summary: Helen Stoner consults Holmes in terror that she will die as her twin Julia did two years earlier after hearing a midnight whistle and crying of 'the speckled band' in a locked room. Holmes inspects the bedrooms at Stoke Moran and finds a dummy bell-rope, a ventilator into Dr. Roylott's room, and a clamped bed revealing a murder method motivated by the mother's will. Keeping a night vigil, Holmes drives Roylott's trained swamp adder back through the ventilator, where it fatally bites Roylott hims
chapters.cover_description: Dr. Grimesby Roylott slumped dead in a wooden chair in his lamplit bedroom, staring rigidly upward with a yellow-brown speckled swamp adder coiled tightly around his brow, while Sherlock Holmes stands at arm's length snaring it with a looped dog-whip beside an open iron safe and a dark-lantern.

chapters.title: THE ADVENTURE OF THE ENGINEER’S THUMB
chapters.summary: Hydraulic engineer Victor Hatherley comes to Watson with his thumb hacked off and tells Holmes of a midnight commission from Colonel Lysander Stark to fix a secret press in the country, where he was nearly crushed, warned by a woman, and maimed escaping from a window. Holmes deduces the press is for large-scale coining and traces the twelve-mile drive to nearby Eyford. The gang has fled and burned the house, leaving only a severed thumb, coining metal, and ruined machinery.
chapters.cover_description: A pale young engineer hanging by his hands from a moonlit bedroom window of a dark country house as a thin sinister man lunges with a butcher's cleaver, rose-bushes and gravel drive below.

chapters.title: THE ADVENTURE OF THE NOBLE BACHELOR
chapters.summary: Lord Robert St. Simon consults Holmes after his Californian bride Hatty Doran vanishes from her wedding breakfast at Lancaster Gate. Holmes deduces from the dropped bouquet, pew stranger, and claim-jumping remark that she fled with an American former lover-husband, tracing Francis Hay Moulton via a hotel bill found with her Serpentine clothes. The reunited Moultons confront the outraged lord in Baker Street, who coldly refuses forgiveness and leaves.
chapters.cover_description: A foppish aristocratic bridegroom in morning coat confronting his missing Californian bride in wedding dress and her sun-browned American husband inside a Victorian Baker Street sitting room laid with a lavish cold supper, firelight and autumn rain at the windows.

chapters.title: THE ADVENTURE OF THE BERYL CORONET
chapters.summary: Banker Alexander Holder leaves the priceless Beryl Coronet as security for a secret 50,000-pound loan and is ruined when his son Arthur is caught at night holding it with three gems missing. Holmes investigates the snow tracks at Fairbank in Streatham and proves Arthur is innocent, having chased thief Sir George Burnwell to rescue the coronet passed out the window by Holder's niece Mary, Burnwell's lover and tool. Holmes buys back the missing stones from a receiver and returns them, while Mary f
chapters.cover_description: At 2 a.m. in a lamplit Victorian dressing-room, a wild young man in only shirt and trousers stands frozen holding a glittering gold coronet set with large beryls, while a portly older banker in nightclothes snatches at it in horror.

chapters.title: THE ADVENTURE OF THE COPPER BEECHES
chapters.summary: Governess Violet Hunter consults Holmes about Rucastle's extravagant offer of £120 a year conditioned on cutting her chestnut hair, wearing an electric-blue dress, and sitting laughing in the window. After she accepts, strange window performances, a watcher on the road, a starved mastiff, a duplicate coil of her hair, and a barricaded lit room in the empty wing terrify her into telegraphing Holmes to Winchester. Holmes deduces she was hired to impersonate the imprisoned daughter Alice Rucastle t
chapters.cover_description: A large whitewashed square country house fronted by a clump of dark copper beeches, with a young chestnut-haired governess in an electric-blue dress laughing in the central front window while a small bearded man watches from the road beyond, and a giant tawny mastiff patrolling the moonlit lawn.
